hero.title: Ask your numbers a question. Get an answer you can check.
hero.subtitle: Analyst reads your warehouse, uses your approved metric definitions and shows the SQL behind every answer. No new dashboards to maintain.

churn.question: Why did churn spike in October?
churn.answer: Churn rose to 4.6% in October, up from 3.4%. 71% of the extra cancellations were annual plans billed through one payment provider that started declining renewals on Oct 9. Excluding them, churn was 3.3%.

regions.question: Which regions drove new revenue this quarter?
regions.answer: DACH led with €412k of new revenue (35% of the total), followed by the Nordics. Iberia is the only region below its target, at 61% of plan.

forecast.question: Are we on track for the Q4 signup target?
forecast.answer: Yes, if the last three weeks hold: weekly signups are trending to 97% of target by week 49. The forecast range is 91–102%.

finance.question: What moved gross margin between September and October?
finance.answer: A bridge: +1.2 pts from pricing, −0.8 pts from cloud costs, −0.3 pts from refunds, with the three largest accounts behind each line.

sales.question: Which deals over €50k have had no activity in 14 days?
sales.answer: Seven deals worth €612k, sorted by close date, with the owner and the last touch for each.

product.question: Did the new onboarding change week-one retention?
product.answer: Week-one retention is 41% for the new flow vs 34% for the old one, across 2,940 signups; the difference holds on mobile and desktop.

support.question: Which features generate the most tickets per active user?
support.answer: Exports and SSO setup, at 3.1 and 2.4 tickets per 100 active users, both trending up since the October release.

business.name: Business
business.for: For companies with a data team

q1.q: Does Analyst train on our data?
q1.a: No. Your data and questions are never used to train models. Queries run read-only against your warehouse and results are kept for 30 days unless you change it.

q2.a: Every answer shows the metric definition and SQL it used, so anyone can check it. Mark an answer as wrong and your data team sees it in a review queue.

q3.q: Do we need a semantic layer first?
q3.a: No. Analyst can start from your existing dbt models or from a few hand-written metrics, and suggests definitions as questions come in.

q4.a: Questions in English, Spanish, German, French and Portuguese. Answers come back in the language of the question.
